title: Decoding Cancer-Associated Mutations in DNA Polymerase eta through Atomistic Simulations.
authors: Visigalli, Alessia; Carloni, Paolo; De Vivo, Marco
journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子动力学模拟研究DNA聚合酶eta癌症相关突变对蛋白-DNA结合稳定性的影响，属于广义蛋白-DNA互作体系，但对象为聚合酶而非转录因子，方法为MD模拟，可借鉴其互作机制建模思路。
abstract: DNA polymerases (Pols) are essential enzymes for DNA replication within the cell. However, DNA lesions, such as cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPDs) induced by ultraviolet (UV) radiation, can impair Pols's function and DNA replication. Therefore, the presence of CPDs can, for example, lead to xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XP-V), a rare genetic disorder characterized by an increased risk of skin cancer. Nonetheless, in these situations, specific translesion synthesis (TLS) Pols, such as human DNA polymerase eta (Poleta), can overcome such lesions, enabling DNA polymerization. That is, Poleta prevents the pathological risks associated with CPD-caused DNA replication stalling. Here, we analyzed how a selected set of 8 Poleta mutations perturbs its structure, DNA binding, and substrate translocation, thereby altering Poleta function, preventing it from bypassing CPDs, thus making them XP-V pathogenic mutations. Leveraging recent structural and clinical data on these pathogenic Poleta variants, we elucidated the mechanistic basis for their impairment of Poleta's ability to bypass damage. We employed molecular dynamics simulations to examine their effects on Poleta in pre- and post-translocation states. Although these residues vary in location and chemical nature, we found that all contributed to reducing DNA anchoring to Poleta. In this way, we could identify a unified mechanistic framework for decoding how XP-V pathogenic mutations compromise Poleta function by destabilizing the Poleta-DNA complex.
abstract_zh: DNA聚合酶（DNA polymerases, Pols）是细胞内DNA复制所必需的酶。然而，DNA损伤，如由紫外线（UV）辐射诱导的环丁烷嘧啶二聚体（cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers, CPDs），可损害Pols的功能和DNA复制。因此，CPDs的存在例如可导致着色性干皮病变异型（xeroderma pigmentosum variant, XP-V），这是一种罕见的遗传性疾病，其特征是皮肤癌风险增加。尽管如此，在这些情况下，特定的跨损伤合成（translesion synthesis, TLS）聚合酶，如人DNA聚合酶eta（Poleta），能够克服此类损伤，实现DNA聚合。即，Poleta可预防与CPD引起的DNA复制停滞相关的病理风险。在此，我们分析了选定的一组8个Poleta突变如何扰动其结构、DNA结合和底物转位，从而改变Poleta功能，阻止其绕过CPDs，使其成为XP-V致病突变。利用这些致病性Poleta变体的近期结构和临床数据，我们阐明了它们损害Poleta损伤绕过能力的机制基础。我们采用分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟来检查它们对Poleta在转位前和转位后状态的影响。尽管这些残基在位置和化学性质上各不相同，但我们发现它们都促进了DNA锚定到Poleta的减少。通过这种方式，我们能够识别一个统一的机制框架，用于解码XP-V致病突变如何通过 destabilizing Poleta-DNA复合物来损害Poleta功能。
